questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to experience what it was like to go to a north american university.
University of Toronto had an interesting selection of courses, which weren't available at my home institution or at many other universities.
A good Anthropology Department.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The process was quite simple as it is quite easy to study in Canada for a Dane.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There were various presentations held via zoom that introduced international students to important aspects of studying and living in Canada. 
Introduction to both housing and health care in Canada, with options for more information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of competition for housing in Toronto. In general it is quite an expensive place to live and it is a good idea to look for a place early on. The university housing is prioritised for permanent students and thus not easily accesible for international short-term students.
Unfortunately the place i had found cancelled on me 2 weeks prior to arrival which made the whole process more difficult, even then i was able to find a place to stay via a Homestay service, which was a fairly cheap option.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Toronto is a big city, so you can easily end up living quite far from campus, the public transportation is decent so that makes it easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university course list was available online, though quite late comparative to the pre-acceptance process at the home university, which caused some minor problems. When released however the registration was fairly easy there was several different registration periods, were you had to fill out a google doc with your desired courses. You could change courses and drop them even after the beginning of the term.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an online presentation with all the necessary information, if needed you could also e-mail the office who were very responsive and helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to register for courses in the first round as that is when it is easiest to get them. Don't be nervous about registering for quite a few as it is easy to drop them if you change your mind, though ideally before the courses begin.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took some 2nd and 3rd year courses, the 2nd years being outside of my main field. I found the general level quite good if a little lower then what i am used to at my home institution. The courses in general were quite forgiving with botht the amount and the level of the readings being a bit lower. The courses i took were quite general and thus there was some overlap with things i had learned about prior.
The courses outside of my main field were quite easy to follow and i definitely recommend them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There were quite classic 2-hour lectures and some group instructions. There was a greater emphasis on interaction between students and professor in the lectures, but less talk with the person sitting next to you. Also note that you are graded on participation much like in Gymnasiet. The instruction were a bit strange they were more like an extension of the lecture with relatively little option for working with other students, they were also quite short only 1 hour.
There is a much greater focus on home work, with at least four different papers written in each class which alongside the exam make up the bulk of your final grade. I found the papers a bit strange to write, it was difficult to reach the level of abstraction usually expected in exams in Denmark and at times they felt like busywork, which took up a lot of time for very little return.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANT344H1 F: Political Anthropology
ANT384H1 F: Special Topics in Society, Culture and Language
HIS264H1 F: Critical Issues in Canadian History
PHL269H1 F: Philosophy of Race

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all the courses, but in particular Philosophy of Race and Special Topic in Society, Culture and Language. These were really interesting and gave a perspective very different from one you usually get in Denmark.
The two other courses were good as well but the was quite a bit of overlap between the Political Anthropology and thing things i had already learned about on the Anthropology Bachelor in Denmark.
The Canadian history course was interesting if you want to learn more about Canada and it's history but really is designed towards Canadian students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay health care insurance to study at the University, they offer a plan. Transportation is a must, the inner city is navigateable by foot or bike, but outside of the center most things are designed around cars and if you don't have one busses of subway.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Celluar service and data are incredibly expensive in Canada, try and get a plan from Denmark. In general prices are quite simmilar to Denmark, drinks, snacks and going out to eat is cheaper, whilst groceries are more expensive. Transportation system is fairly cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything honestly, there is a great culture around student driven clubs and activities, so you can find pretty much anything and everything that interests you.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I took part in some board game and some movie clubs which were really nice. There also is a camping and outdoors club which is nice for exploring a bit outside the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are some nice museums and like in Toronto. Toronto in general is massive and has lots to offer. Try to watch some university sports teams it's free and a pretty fun experience even if you're not into sports. Also explore a bit outside the city or visit Montreal, Niagara Falls or even the US. Things are a bit further away but Toronto is fairly well-connected to the sorroundings.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy. Canadians are in general quite friendly and polite, there is a lot more small talk and conversation everywhere which can be scary for introverted danes, but it's ok. Everyone speaks english and many people do it with accents so don't be nervous about how you speak it is easy to understand one another. 
There are lots of cars and Canada in general is built around having them so it's a little trickier to get around if you don't have one especially outside the city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't know if i did. Maybe the time difference but you get used to it quickly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are generally nice and friendly and open-minded. It's a very multicultural society that's open to people. Canadian culture seems to be the culture of many different peoples and that was nice to experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be too nervous it's a nice place with a high quality of education and friendly people
Try and find a place to stay early on, it helps.
Do things outside of education as well, it is supposed to be an experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really. Have fun!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a completly different place and culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to stay two weeks before going.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
